clue.text: Frankly only having eleven players

definitions.meaning: speaking frankly means holding nothing back, quite openly
a football or cricket side of exactly eleven has no substitute in hand

explanation.surface: A remark about a short-handed team, delivered with candour.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something openly and fully is an idiom for candour, and a side with no substitutes literally lacks a spare player.

clue.text: Cricketer up about ten with one accountant in the vehicle

indicators.note: the turned word goes around the other pieces
in a down clue the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: a bat is a batsman, a cricketer
X is the Roman numeral ten
I is one
CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: A cricketer, an accountant and others crammed into a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns BAT into TAB, which goes 'about' X, I and CA.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxicab is a hired car, a vehicle for fares.

clue.text: Former pupil to look up a silver coin

parts.note: OB is an old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is read upwards

parts.note: lo means look!

explanation.surface: An old boy looks for a silver coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The obol was a small silver coin of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Tear round with broken-down bike to see end of tennis set?

indicators.note: the letters go round, turning into a new order
the bike is broken, its letters wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone races round on a clapped-out bike to watch tennis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' and 'broken-down' both work on TEAR and BIKE together.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-break is the deciding game that concludes a tennis set at six all.

clue.text: Car for one's total possessions?

definitions.meaning: a car with a rear loading space
all one owns, especially at death

explanation.surface: A will leaves the car and everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: A station wagon is the British name for this car; a person's property in law is the same word.

clue.text: All three vying desperately

indicators.note: the competing is frantic, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Three people compete frantically.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole lot, every item, is a synonym for all.

clue.text: French town fashionable for serf

parts.note: ville is French for town
in means in fashion

explanation.surface: A fashionable French town for a peasant.
explanation.definitionFit: A villein was a feudal tenant tied to the land, a serf.

clue.text: Finally free with nothing to do?

definitions.text: Finally free with nothing to do?

parts.words: Finally free with nothing to do?
parts.note: a phrase for idleness, read as a rope end that is untied and loose

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means idle, unoccupied, likened to an untied rope end.

clue.text: Interpreter was on first page of the book

parts.note: ex- means former, something that was
first is number one
NT is the New Testament, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A translator was mentioned right at the start of the volume.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces run EX, P, ONE, NT; 'on' and 'of the' only join them.
explanation.definitionFit: An exponent is someone who expounds or performs a work, so an interpreter of it.

clue.text: Ale, it was mixed to produce port!

indicators.note: the letters of the drink and the pronoun are stirred together into a new order

explanation.surface: A drinker mixes beer and ends up with a fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' suggests the drink after 'Ale'; it is a harbour town, Israel's Red Sea port.
explanation.definitionFit: Eilat is Israel's harbour city on the Gulf of Aqaba.

clue.text: Bird not welcomed by yachtsmen

parts.note: split in three, the bird's name describes a dark stormy spell at sea that sailors dread

explanation.definitionFit: The songbird famed for singing after dark splits as being out after dark in a storm.

clue.text: Long Island? Hardly

parts.note: a Scots word for a small island is also a tiny unit of length, so it is an island but hardly long

explanation.walkthrough: In Scotland a small island is called an inch (Inchcolm, Inchkeith), and an inch is far from long.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a small Scottish isle and a very short measure of length.

clue.text: Not exactly charming by spring

parts.note: charming means pretty, attractive
a spring is a well, a source of water

explanation.surface: Someone admires an attractive spring, though not wholeheartedly.
explanation.definitionFit: 'More or less, nearly' is the sense of the idiom, which means not exactly.

clue.text: The way one moans about the builder

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: the words are moved about, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone complains about a builder on the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A mason working with stone is a builder in masonry.

clue.text: Usual practice is socially acceptable by a student

parts.note: a practice is a habit, a custom
U means upper-class, socially acceptable
L is a learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A remark that a student's routine conduct is perfectly proper.
explanation.walkthrough: U (upper-class usage) is an old British label for what is socially acceptable; L is the learner plate on a British learner driver's car.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done regularly by custom is the ordinary or customary thing.

clue.text: Younger boy endlessly includes clue about a Japanese religion

indicators.note: the shortened word holds the clue synonym within it
the son loses his final letter, so the word has no end

parts.note: a son is a younger boy of the family
a clue is a hint

explanation.surface: A boy offers a puzzle hint about an Eastern faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts SON to SO, and 'includes' puts HINT inside it; 'about' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Shinto is the indigenous faith of Japan, worshipping kami spirits.

clue.text: Was in contact with Joseph at home amongst dead-letters to be sorted

indicators.note: the short name and home word sit among the shuffled letters
the letters need sorting, so they are rearranged

parts.note: Jo is a short form of Joseph
in means at home

explanation.surface: A postal worker sorts undelivered mail with Joseph at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be sorted' turns DEAD into AD ED, and 'amongst' puts JO and IN between; 'letters' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjoined means bordered on, touched, so was in contact with.

clue.text: It is extremely foolish to be in the said waterway in France

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the river is spoken and the sound gives a word for rational

parts.note: the Seine is the river through Paris

explanation.surface: Someone thinks it mad to go swimming in a French river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It is' and 'to be' are links; the Seine said out loud gives SANE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out of one's mind is very foolish, the everyday sense of mad.

clue.text: Material, it's a net product

indicators.note: the net is a thing produced, so its letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: A fabric described as the outcome of netting.
explanation.definitionFit: Satinet is a thin imitation satin fabric.

clue.text: Old garden gallery lacking teeth

parts.note: Eden is the ancient garden of Genesis
the Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.surface: An ancient garden and an art gallery, both somehow toothless.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a famous art gallery in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Edentate is the zoological term for animals with no or few teeth, like sloths.

clue.text: Woman's suitor married stranger

indicators.note: stranger here means odder, so the letters are made odd and rearranged

explanation.surface: A married man has a mystery admirer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stranger' looks like a noun but is the comparative of strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone courting a woman is her admirer.

clue.text: Welcomes with a word of thanks the sacred writings

parts.note: aves are greetings, hails
ta is British slang for thanks

explanation.surface: A thank-you greets the holy texts.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: The Avesta is the scripture of Zoroastrianism.

clue.text: Instruction to hurry at chess?

parts.note: an order to be quick, read literally as a command to a slow chess player to make his turn

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom urges haste, and in chess a turn is literally a move.

clue.text: Nothing on island near Saudi Arabia

parts.note: O is zero, nothing
the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Nothing doing on an island close to the Arabian kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' joins the two pieces; the definition locates the country.
explanation.definitionFit: The sultanate borders the Arabian kingdom on its south-eastern side.

clue.text: French cleric be after the sailor

indicators.note: the verb comes after the seaman

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: A French priest is told to follow a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbe is a French priest or abbot.

clue.text: Joins at the golf club

definitions.meaning: a seaside golf course and club

explanation.surface: Someone becomes a member of a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: To connect is to couple things up; a seaside golf course is called by the same word.

clue.text: Musical airborne traveller?

parts.note: a flier that makes tunes, read as a melodic winged creature

explanation.definitionFit: A singing bird such as a thrush is a tuneful flier.

clue.text: Prominent leader of a cause carries the flag

definitions.meaning: a figurehead who leads a movement
one who literally bears a banner

explanation.surface: A campaign leader marches ahead holding the banner.
explanation.definitionFit: A banner holder in battle led the troops, giving the figurative sense of a movement's champion.
